title: AngularLynx dev-server builder
description: Runs the rspeedy dev server, which Lynx Explorer and the web preview load the app from.

buildTarget.description: The build target to serve, as `project:target[:configuration]`, e.g. `my-app:build:development`. Its options (the Angular compiler options, `config`) configure the build, and its `optimization` picks a production or development build. Defaults to the project's build target with its development configuration, as Angular's own dev server does.

port.description: The port to serve on. Overrides `server.port` in lynx.config.ts.

host.description: The host to listen on. Overrides `server.host` in lynx.config.ts.

environment.description: Only build these rspeedy environments (e.g. lynx). Defaults to the build target's `environment`, or all of them.

platform.description: Also build the app's development build for this platform, from the build target's native options (appId, icon, permissions, ...), and open it on a simulator, emulator or phone, as `ng build --platform <platform> --run` does. It loads the bundle from the dev server and reloads on every edit. Its native build is cached: a second `ng serve` with the same native options opens the app without running Xcode or Gradle.

device.description: With --platform, where to open the app: on iOS a simulator's or a paired iPhone's name (e.g. "iPhone 18 Pro", "Jane's iPhone") or UDID, on Android a virtual device's name or an adb serial (e.g. emulator-5554). Without it, iOS uses the running simulator, or else starts the newest iPhone simulator; Android uses the running emulator or connected phone, or else starts the first virtual device. An iPhone needs ios.teamId.
